rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Harm the rule prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader and leaks strategy-doc vocabulary into student prose. Present here — 'crucially' is on the ban list and is doing no work the sentence needs. Ran: grep -nEi '\b(crucial|crucially|importantly|honest|delve|substrate|leverag)' over body lines 1-65 → 1 hit, line 5. Em-dash half of the same rule is clean: grep -n '—' over body lines 1-65 → 0 hits.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the adverb; the sentence is a candidate for deletion outright (see check_student_facing 33 row).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: L11: 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' Harm: ceremony vocabulary reframes an exercise as a Scrum-style ritual, exactly the register the training exists to replace. Present, and doubly so — the word is hard-banned AND the claim is false for this file (the maintainer block at L70 places it as an in-class M1 exercise, third of four, not a per-session repeat). Ran: grep -nEi '\b(ritual|ceremony|practice)\b' over body lines 1-65 → 1 hit, line 11.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence. If a repeat-move is genuinely wanted, it is a different claim and belongs in a different beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L49: 'This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.' Harm: changelog in place of rules — a reader who never saw the previous version loses nothing if the clause vanishes, which is the rule's own tense test, and here the clause states only a transition. Present in the strongest form: transition verb ('previously', 'was fixed') plus a bare date, in student-facing body, not in a maintainer block where the dated-provenance carve-out lives. Ran: grep -nEi '\b(previously|used to|no longer|was fixed|now fixed|retired)\b|20[0-9][0-9]-' over body lines 1-65 → 1 hit, line 49.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the whole sentence; git blame carries the provenance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three body lines sit outside the AE101 voice quintet (Boris / Martin / Godin / Sutherland / Siilasmaa). L11 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' and L37 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' are both L&D-coach register, which the rule names as the wrong register by example. L5 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' is emphasis-by-adverb where Boris-direct would state the mechanism. Harm: decode cost and coach-voice flinch on an engineer audience whose contract is 'write to the caution' — none of the three gives the caution a job. Closest passing line for contrast: L28 'Every field carries a convention.' — flat, factual, Boris.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The three coach-register lines are the same edit as their own rule rows: cut them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner move is paraphrased in body and no creator name appears. Ran: grep -nE '\bAntti\b|\bthe creator\b|\bthe author\b|\bcourse creator\b|\btraining creator\b' over body lines 1-65 → 0 hits (the only 'Antti' strings in the file are at L72 and L87-onward, below the maintainer cut at L66). Author-we sub-rule also clean: no body sentence opens on 'We'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L24: 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' Harm: third-person teacher voice in student-facing body — the reader is addressed as a case being taught rather than as the person doing the work, and the sentence is delivery mechanics the rule routes below the maintainer fence. Present, and not covered by the Connections room-harvest carve-out (this is neither a Connections section nor a room read). Ran: grep -nE '\bthe student\b' over body lines 1-65 → 1 hit, line 24.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete it. Recasting to 'you' does not save it — see the check_student_facing 27 row for why the claim itself is wrong here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L37: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' Harm: reassurance-shaped prose signals the author thought the beat needed defending; the rule's own flag list carries 'no penalty' and 'fine way to' verbatim. Present, and compounded — the sentence sits directly above L39 'Push back on the five.', so the file reassures the reader that a beat is optional and then instructs them to do it two lines later.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; the push-back line already carries the whole instruction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call is L53 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' — bare 'it' with the close-out, the ticket update and the agent's report all live in the preceding beat. It stays inside because the section header at L51, 'Double-check the voice', fixes the referent to the close-out's wording one line above. Recorded because it is close, and because the same line does fail check_student_facing 9 on a different axis.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it
rules_evaluated.evidence: Block present at L60-64 and clears the three moves: count plus noun at L62 ('Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note …, and the conventions …'), one qualifier on what makes it the reader's ('your team has been encoding in its fields all along'), destination at L64 ('The field rules stay in the scrollback.'). Past tense throughout ('came out', 'closed'), per the recap-tense clause. 47 words across two sentences, at the top of the 25-40 band but not a replay.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62 'Two things came out of one ticket:' states a count immediately above the two items it enumerates, which is the shape this rule bans. It stays because rule 16's move 1 prescribes exactly that shape for a What happened block — 'Count + noun, artifact as grammatical subject, numeral doing the work' — and the more specific rule governs. Recording the collision rather than filing it: a fix here would break rule 16.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L53 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' is the only how-you-know clause in the body, and it points at an external observation that can come back negative — the comments already on the ticket, written before this session. Not self-witnessing: the agent's own draft is not the judge of the agent's own draft.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43 'Adding a connector is one command per tracker.' uses 'connector' cold, with no one-breath primer. It stays: the file's maintainer block at L72 carries an explicit accept-note ('"Connector" is assumed-known vocabulary (Antti 2026-08-18) … findings on it are overruled, do not re-file'), and the rule's own assumed-known carve-out routes the call to the AE101 engineer audience tier. No other unearned term in body — 'tracker', 'repro steps', 'CI pipeline', 'API' are all ordinary professional vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L53: 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.' Harm: a LOOK-line owing an object and a tell supplies neither — the object is a bare 'it' rather than the agent's close-out draft, and the tell is a feeling ('feels off or wrong') rather than what a bad instance looks like. This is the exact passage the rule's own text names as under-audited: the register beat in close-the-ticket sits inside this rule's error-catching exemption, so judges mark it exempt and never re-run the actor-and-mechanism clause on the same sentence. Speech verb is correctly addressed ('tell Claude'), so that clause passes; this is the object-and-tell clause failing. Pre-existing, not planted.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the object ('Claude's close-out') and give a concrete tell — the file's own maintainer push at L88 already has one: does it sound like the same team wrote it?

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: One inline link, L43: '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)'. Link text is the target's title, not the filename and not a backticked path. The depth-counted '../' prefix is a path-form question owned by curriculum/module-shape.md, and this rule states explicitly that it governs link TEXT only — a prior judge already mis-filed on that, so it is not filed here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The split holds. Acting → 'the agent' (L18 'The agent will offer to create one.', L29 'The agent separates strong signals from guesses', L58 'Ask the agent to study the pipeline'). Addressee → 'Claude' (L33, L45, L53 all 'Ask Claude to …' / 'tell Claude'). Thinking/capability → 'LLM' once, at L57 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM'. That is the reshape the backing block at L125 records as deliberate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Harm: noun-run for the agent's sitting is banned in student-facing body because it collides with test/CI/eval runs, and this body carries the CI sense nearby (L57 'a CI pipeline'). Present — 'the run' here means the agent working on the task, which is a session. Every other body reference uses the right nouns: L11 'session', L64 'this whole session'.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the sentence survives at all, 'the session' is the word; but see the rule 33 row — the sentence is a deletion candidate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L37: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' Harm: information that changes nothing the student understands, decides, does or notices next — and worse than neutral, since it licenses skipping a beat the very next line instructs them to do. Fails the fastest screen too: that a skipped optional step carries no penalty is obvious to a working engineer. L5 fails the same screen from the other side ('this step matters' is a claim about the curriculum, not a move).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut L37 outright; nothing downstream depends on it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L24: 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' Harm: narrating the reader's own state after a chat-print, with no follow-on move — the ban on generic notice-lines with no direction. Present, and the claim is also false at this arc position: the maintainer block at L70 places this exercise after fix-tests-first, 'the PR is shipped', so the test is green by the time anyone reads L24. A body line asserting a red test two beats after it went green is a fictional observation the student will look for and not find, which costs trust the same way rule 9's fifth axis describes.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the line. There is no salvageable version — the state it narrates does not exist here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Harm: maintainer cartography wearing an orientation face — the grammatical subject is 'the step', an exercise beat, not the student's ticket, agent, artifact or decision. Runs the deletion test: remove L5 and L3 ('**Time:** 20 minutes.') joins L7 ('**What you do:** read one real ticket …') cleanly, losing nothing. Sits outside every exemption — this is not Big Idea, What You'll Learn, Connections, Bridge/Next or Prework. Closest passing neighbour: L13 '**The point:** the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules.' names what the module earns rather than where the beat sits, and is exempt by name.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence rather than de-adverbing it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 M1's slot in the mood arc is earned-trust / curious-readiness. L11's ceremony framing and L37's reassurance both push the beat toward compliance-and-permission, and L24's teacher-observation ('the student should notice') seats the reader as an observed pupil. None of the three is a garnish failure alone; together they move the module's felt register off its target, which is why they are recorded here as well as under their word-level rules.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cutting L11, L24 and L37 restores the arc position; no replacement prose is owed.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned word 'crucially' — consultancy register that flinches an engineer reader. The same line also narrates the curriculum's own shape (check_student_facing 33) and uses the banned noun-run for a session (check_student_facing 21b).

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned ceremony vocabulary, and factually wrong for this file — the maintainer block places it as an in-class M1 exercise, third of four, not a per-session repeat.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher framing in student-facing body, plus delivery mechanics that belong below the maintainer fence. The observation is also false at this arc position: this exercise runs after fix-tests-first, where the PR is already shipped.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Dated 'fixed' retrospective in student-facing prose — changelog where a rule belongs. A reader who never saw the previous version loses nothing if it vanishes, which is the rule's own tense test.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence; git blame carries provenance.

findings.quote: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.
findings.harm: Reassurance-shaped hedge on the rule's own flag list ('no penalty'), and it contradicts L39 'Push back on the five.' two lines below.

findings.quote: Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.
findings.harm: Pre-existing, not planted. The LOOK-line names no object (bare 'it') and its tell is a feeling rather than what a bad instance looks like. This is the passage the rule's own text cites as the one judges bless under the error-catching exemption and never re-check.
findings.fix: Name the object ('Claude's close-out') and borrow the concrete tell already in the maintainer block at L88: does it sound like the same team wrote it?

todos.note: Register beat's object-and-tell gap is pre-existing and survives the file's 2026-08-24 writing PASS; worth a maintainer call rather than a silent rewrite, since the rule's own text uses this passage as its worked example.

'Two things came out of one ticket:' is a count adjacent to its own list (writing 20) and simultaneously the prescribed move-1 shape for a What happened block (writing 16). Filed as PASS under the more specific rule; the collision is worth one line in whichever compendium wants to own it.

'The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' is a later-module predicate, the 2026-08-23 cartography amendment. Not filed: it is doing load-bearing work, telling the reader no rules-file write is owed here, which the maintainer block at L70 records as deliberate design. Rule question rather than a finding.
